paragraphs.text: Form No.HCJD/C-121 ORDER SHEET IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, MULTAN BENCH, MULTAN. JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT C.M.No.3140 of 2023 [u/s 12(2) C.P.C.] Province of Punjab etc. Versus Hafiz Abdul Aziz etc. In Writ Petition No.12069 of 2010 Hafiz Abdul Aziz etc. Vs. Province of Punjab etc. Sr.No. of Order/ Proceeding Date of Order/ Proceeding Order with signatures of Judge and that of parties or counsel, where necessary. 14.09.2026 Kunwar Sajid Ali, Assistant Advocate General for the applicants. Mr. Saif Ullah Khan, Advocate for the respondents. Malik Muhammad Ali Dhol and Syed Tajammul Hussain Bukhari, Advocate for the respondents. Through this single order, I intend to decide three applications under Section 12(2) CPC which are as under:- i) C.M.No.3140 of 2023 [u/s 12(2) C.P.C.] in [Writ Petition No.12069/2010], ii) C.M.No.3138 of 2023 [u/s 12(2) C.P.C.] in Writ Petition No.9563/2010 & iii) C.M.No.3142 of 2023 [u/s 12(2) C.P.C.] in Writ Petition No.9372/2010 as common questions of law and facts are involved in these cases.

Through the aforesaid applications under Sections 12(2) CPC the applicants/Province of Punjab etc. have challenged the vires of consolidated judgment dated 14.12.2010 [announced on 21.12.2010] passed in Writ Petitions No.12069/2010, No.9563/2010 & No.9372/2010 reported as Muhammad Zafar & 7 Others Vs Member (Judicial-V), Board of Revenue, Punjab, & 3 Others (2011 MLD 1059). C.M.No.3140 of 2023 [u/s 12(2) C.P.C.] In W.P.No.12069-2010.

Brief facts of the case are that respondents No.1 to 4 filed Writ Petition No.12069 of 2010 with the contentions that Allah Bakhsh grandfather of respondents No.1 to 4 was retired as Tehsil Jamadar. He obtained lease of state land measuring 49-acres, 09-pole, situated in Rakh Kotla Sikhani later on, named as Mouza Kotla Sikhani Gharbi, Tehsil DG Khan vide order dated 04.03.1908 issued by the Financial Commissioner Punjab Lahore. Said lessee/Allah Bakhsh passed away and his inheritance mutation was incorporated in the Record through mutation No.1401 dated 19.11.1984 in the name of his only son Abdul Aziz. After the death of Allah Bakhsh, the lease rights were transferred in favour of respondents No.2 to 4 as his grandson and granddaughters from his daughter Mst. Allah Wasai through inheritance mutation No.1567 dated 11.12.1985. Respondents No.2 to 4 filed an application for grant of proprietary rights on 13.12.1995 to the Assistant Commissioner/Collector, DG Khan who declared the respondents entitled to get proprietary rights. But the District Officer (Revenue), DG Khan dismissed the said application vide order dated 11.03.2005. Respondents No.2 to 4 assailed the said order through an appeal which was dismissed by the Executive District Officer (Revenue), DG Khan vide order dated 17.03.2010. Against the above said orders, respondents No.2 to 4 filed a revision petition before the Member Board of Revenue who dismissed the said petition vide order dated 20.08.2010. The aforesaid orders of the Revenue hierarchy were assailed through the Writ Petition No.12069/2010 which was allowed vide judgment dated 14.12.2010 [announced on 21.12.2010]. The Member Board of Revenue, Punjab challenged the said judgment through an Intra Court Appeal [No.208/2011] which was dismissed being barred by limitation by the learned Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 21.06.2012. The said order was assailed by the Member Board of Revenue through CPLAs No.297-L of 2011, 1735-L & 1776- L of 2012 which were dismissed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan vide order dated 11.03.2015 being barred by law. Civil Petition No.1732-L/12 of the Member Board of Revenue was also dismissed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan vide judgment dated 29.06.2016. C.M.No.3138 of 2023 [u/s 12(2) C.P.C.] in Writ Petition No.9563/2010

In the above application the facts in brevity are that the respondents filed Writ Petition No.9563/2010 against the applicants contending therein that the grandfather of the respondents and proforma applicant No.7 namely Mian Abdul Hakeem was then Inspector of Police. He was leased out waste state land measuring 196-acres (1530-Kanals) situated in Mouza Kotla Sukhani Gharbi, Tehsil & District DG Khan by the then Financial Commissioner, Punjab vide lease deed dated 22.02.1908. That said lessee Mian Abdul Hakeem, died in 1914 leaving behind two sons namely Qadir Bakhsh and Abdul Karim. Respondents No.1 & 2 [petitioners No.1 & 2 in the Writ Petition] are legal heirs of Qadir Bakhsh, while remaining respondents [petitioners in the Writ Petition] are legal heirs of Abdul Karim. Qadir Bakhsh died in the year 1967 and his inheritance mutation No.245 was attested on 24.03.1969 in favour of respondents No.1 and 2, whereas Abdul Karim died in the year 1986 and his inheritance mutation No.294 was sanctioned on 20.03.1989 in favour of respondents No.3 to 9. The legal heirs of Qadir Bakhsh and Abdul Karim filed applications for getting proprietary rights of the state land which were dismissed by the District Officer (Revenue)/District Collector, DG Khan vide order dated 11.03.2005. Against the said dismissal order respondents and others filed six appeals which were dismissed by the Executive District Officer (Revenue), DG Khan vide order dated 17.03.2010. Against the said order, respondents filed ROR Nos.56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 65 of 2010 & No.1290 of 2008 which were also dismissed by the Member (Judicial-V), Board of Revenue, Punjab vide order dated 20.08.2010. The aforementioned orders were challenged by the respondents through Writ Petition No.9563/2010 which was allowed vide judgment dated 14.12.2010 [announced on 21.12.2010]. Hence, this application. C.M.No.3142 of 2023 [u/s 12(2) C.P.C.] in Writ Petition No.9372/2010

The salient facts of this application are that the respondents filed Writ Petition No.9372/2010 against the applicants and proforma respondents No.9 & 10 with the assertions that Ghulam Muhammad predecessor in interest of the respondents was tenant over land measuring 318- Kanals situated in Mouza Kotla Sikhani Gharbi, Tehsil DG Khan, the detail whereof is mentioned in Para No.2 of the Writ Petition. The Settlement Officer, DG Khan vide order dated 06.02.1989 granted proprietary rights of land measuring 79-1/2 Bigas in Kotla Sikhani Gharbi and conveyance deed was executed on 26.02.1989 and on the basis of conveyance deed dated 26.02.1989 mutations No.283 and 284 dated 28.02.1989 were sanctioned in the names of respondents No.1 to 8 and possession was also handed over to them; that vide letter dated 21.10.1990, the Deputy Commissioner/Settlement Officer initiated review proceedings to examine the legality, propriety and correctness of grant of proprietary rights to the said respondents who after perusing the record refused to review the order of granting proprietary rights dated 06.02.1989. Likewise Allah Ditta son of Imam Bakhsh and others also filed an application for grant of proprietary rights and the Deputy Commissioner /Settlement Officer refused to grant proprietary rights to them. They filed Writ Petition No.119/1993 which was heard alongwith with Writ Petition No.43-R/1993 and the same were disposed of vide judgment dated 27.03.2001 and cases of Allah Ditta and others were remanded to the Deputy Commissioner/Settlement Officer, DG Khan to look into matter regarding any discrimination and their locus poenitentiae qua the claimant in Writ Petition No.119/1993, Deputy Commissioner cancelled conferment of proprietary rights vide order dated 06.02.1989 in favour of respondents No.1 to 8 Feeling aggrieved, respondents No.1 to 8 filed Writ Petition No.43-R/1993 and this Court vide judgment dated 27.03.2001 disposed of the Writ Petition and referred the matter to the Member (Colonies), Board of Revenue, Punjab. In post remand proceedings the Member vide order dated 03.09.2004 dismissed the revision petitions and upheld the order dated 19.10.1993 passed by the District Collector, DG Khan. Ghulam Muhammad, predecessor of respondents No.1 to 8 filed Writ Petition No.5496- R/2004 which was disposed of by this Court vide order dated 13.10.2004 and upheld the order dated 03.09.2004 of Member Board of Revenue. Against the above decision said Ghulam Muhammad filed Civil Appeal No.768/2006 before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan but withdrew the same vide order dated 26.09.2006. Thus the said issue is set at rest infinitum. Later on, respondent No.8/Mst. Rafia Naz daughter of Ghulam Muhammad filed an application for grant of proprietary rights under the policy dated 28.05.1995 which was dismissed by the District Officer (Revenue), DG Khan vide order dated 11.03.2005. Against the said orders, Ghulam Muhammad, predecessor of the respondents filed an appeal which was also dismissed by the Executive District Officer (Revenue), DG Khan vide order dated 17.03.2010. Against the above said adverse orders a Revision Petition (ROR No.1290/2008) was preferred by the respondents which was also dismissed by the Member Board of Revenue vide order dated 20.08.2010. Respondents challenged the said order through Writ Petition No.9372/2010 which was allowed by this Court vide judgment dated 14.12.2010, announced on 21.12.2010 which judgment is questioned in this petition.

The District Bar Association, Dera Ghazi Khan etc. filed Writ Petition No.1253/2015 with the prayer that the respondents in the said petition may be restrained to interfere into their lawful possession. The said Writ Petition was disposed of by this Court vide order dated 23.05.2022 with the direction as under:- “The precise submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner is upon a judgment passed by this Court reported as Muhammad Zafar and 7 others Vs. Member (Judicial-V), Board of Revenue Punjab and 3 others (2011 MLD 1059) in which respondents have admitted the transfer of land in favour of the petitioner Bar Association. The only grievance in this petition is regarding the failure on the part of the respondents to follow up on the documentation of that transfer. Learned Additional Advocate General submits that petition for leave to appeal is pending with the Supreme Court of Pakistan and so the order could not be implemented. He also relies upon a subsequent notification issued by the Board of Revenue which bars any transfer of state land without process of having it auctioned. Be that as it may, these issues were determined by the learned Single Judge in the judgment relied upon by the petitioner and until that judgment is in field, it will have to be implemented subject to any decision to the contrary passed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan. This petition is, therefore, disposed of with a direction that transfer of land and the necessary documentation in this regard shall be made within next one month from the receipt of the order of this Court by the relevant respondents. It has been informed that determination of cost of the land has already been made at that time by the respondents and a challan for which shall also be taken out by the respondents to be paid by the Bar Association within reasonable time.”

Another Writ Petition No.16817 of 2023 was filed by the District Bar Association, Dera Ghazi Khan etc. praying therein that the Muhammad Zafar’s case1 may be implemented. This Court directed the respondents to implement the said judgment vide order dated 27.10.2023. 1 Muhammad Zafar & 7 Others Vs Member (Judicial-V), Board of Revenue, Punjab, & 3 Others (2011 MLD

The Province of Punjab assailed the above said orders rendered in the aforementioned writ petitions before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan through CPLA No.2372-L/2022 and CPLA No.3844/2023 which CPLAs were converted into Civil appeals vide order dated 13.11.2025 and the order dated 27.10.2023 of this Court was set aside with the direction to this Court to decide the application under Section 12(2) C.P.C. and thereafter, passed appropriate orders in the aforementioned writ petitions. Hence these applications primarily on the ground that Province of Punjab was not arrayed as party to the aforementioned litigation since its inception onward. The state land is situated in the prohibited zone and same cannot be allotted permanently to any lessee/ tenant or any other entity, as such the impugned judgment was obtained through concealment of material facts which are liable to be reversed.
Arguments heard and record perused.

The Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan while deciding CPLA No.2372-L/2022 and CPLA No.3844/2023 filed by the Province of Punjab etc. passed order dated 13.11.2025 as under; “It is reflected from the record that the respondents filed C.P. No.1252/2015 before the learned High Court, Multan Bench, Multan, seeking the following relief: - "Prayer: In the light of above humble submissions, it is most respectfully prayed that this writ petition may kindly be graced with acceptance, the aforesaid illegal act of making interference into the lawful possession of the petitioners body and dispossessing the advocates of Lawyer Colony form the forenoted piece of land, may very graciously be declared to be illegal, malafide, capricious, perverse, arbitrary, preposterous, without lawful authority, without jurisdiction, null and void, against all canons of justice and against fundamental rights of the citizens/petitioners and others, in the supreme interest of justice. It is further prayed that the respondents be directed not to make any kind of interference into the lawful possession of the petitioners or dispossessing them from the forenoted piece of land in the supreme interest of justice. Any other relief under the law which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and appropriate be also awarded in favour of petitioners." 2. After providing right of audience to the learned counsel for the parties, the learned High Court decided the fate of the Constitution Petition in the following manner: - "The precise submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner is upon a judgment passed by this Court reported as Muhammad Zafar and 7 others Vs. Member (Judicial-V], Board of Revenue Punjab and 3 others (2011 MLD 1059) in which respondents have admitted the transfer of land in favour of the petitioner Bar Association. The only grievance in this petition is regarding the failure on the part of the respondents to follow up on the documentation of that transfer. Learned Additional Advocate General submits that petition for leave to appeal is pending with the Supreme Court of Pakistan and so the order could not be implemented. He also relies upon a subsequent notification issued by the Board of Revenue which bars any transfer of state land without process of having it auctioned. Be that as it may, these issues were determined by the learned Single Judge in the judgment relied upon by the petitioner and until that judgment is in field, it will have to be implemented subject to any decision to the contrary passed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan. This petition is, therefore, disposed of with a direction that transfer of land and the necessary documentation in this regard shall be made within next one month from the receipt of the order of this Court by the relevant respondents. It has been informed that determination of cost of the land had already been made at that time by the respondents and a challan for which shall also be taken out by the respondents to be paid by the Bar Association within reasonable time. 3. Being aggrieved of the same, the petitioner has filed the instant petition. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, and going through the record, we are of the view that the following question left unattended by the learned High Court: "Whether the Constitution Petition brought by the respondents was factually and legally maintainable or not, particularly keeping in view the prayer clause and contents of the Constitution Petition." 4. We, therefore, without touching merits of the case, deem it appropriate to set-aside the impugned judgment passed by the learned High Court and remand the case to it for decision afresh keeping in mind the question formulated hereinabove. 5. In view of the above, this petition is converted into appeal and is allowed. C.P.L.A.3844/2023 6. So far as this petition is concerned, it appears from the record that by instituting a Constitution Petition, the respondents sought implementation and execution of the order passed by the learned High Court, Multan Bench in Constitution Petition No.9393/2010, dated 14.12.2010 and subsequent order passed by the learned High Court in Constitution Petition No.1253/2015. After providing right of audience to the learned counsel for the parties, the learned High Court passed the following order: "It will be noted that order was also passed in C.M.No.5519/2023 which was an application made by the Government of Punjab through Government Pleader with the following prayer:- It is, therefore, respectfully prayed that matter of determination of cost of land in issue may kindly be determined ahead of sanction/issuance of the Mutation of subject to the outcome of the CPLA, and Petitioner/District Bar Association may kindly be directed to deposit the same before the Mutation of the land, in the interest of justice." 7. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the parties informed the Court that the petitioner has impugned the original judgment of the learned High Court by filing an application under section 12(2) CPC, which is still sub judice. 8. We, therefore, without touching the merit of the case, direct the learned High Court to decide the fate of the petition filed under section 12(2) CPC within a period of four months positively from the date of receipt of this order and thereafter pass appropriate order in the Constitution Petition brought by the respondents seeking implementation and execution of the earlier order passed by the learned High Court. 9. In view of the above, this petition is converted into appeal and is allowed and the impugned judgment passed by the High Court dated 27.10.2023 is set-aside leaving the High Court at liberty to pass any appropriate order in the Constitution Petition, including interim relief sought by the respondents. Till then the respondents shall not be dispossessed, if not already dispossessed from the property in dispute.”

The main controversy revolvers around the points; “(i). Whether the impugned judgment was obtained through fraud, misrepresentation, want of jurisdiction, concealment of true facts and properly assisting this Court. As the applicants filed applications under Section 12(2) CPC for recalling the judgment passed by this Court, and thus applicants were under mandatory obligation to bring their pleading/ assertion within indispensable parameter of the above provision such as fraud, misrepresentation and want of jurisdiction of the Court.

Before marching ahead, it is appropriate to decide the question of limitation, suffice it to say that existence of fraud in a transaction or order etc. can be inferred from the surrounding circumstances and conduct of the parties, whereas no time limit is prescribed to challenge the fraudulent transaction as any transaction based on fraud is void ab initio and notwithstanding the bar of limitation the matter can be considered on merits and not to allow a fraud to be perpetuated in this respect. As order was obtained on the basis of fraud and concealment of material facts, as such no limitation runs against such void order.2

Admittedly, the Provincial Government is owner of the suit property whereas it was not made party in the said Writ Petitions and the impugned order was obtained from this Court on the basis of concealment of facts whereas Article 174 of the Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 as well as under Section 79, read with Order XXVII of Civil Procedure Code, 1908 mandatorily requires impleading of Province of Punjab through Member (Colonies), Board of Revenue as a party and without arraying it as a party to the lis, no effective decree can be passed and if a decree is passed in violation of the above provisions, that will be inexecutable 2 Nawab Syed Raunaq Ali etc. Vs. Chief Settlement Commissioner & Others (PLD 1973 SC 236), Surriya Bibi & Others Vs Ghulam Sarwar & Others (1999 SCMR 2277), Lahore Development Authority Vs Firdous Steel Mills (Pvt.) Ltd. (2010 SCMR 1097), Pir Shah Abdul Haq (deceased) through L.Rs. & Another Vs Muhammad Irfan & Others (2026 SCMR 1019) and Muhammad Rasheed (Deceased) through his Legal Heirs & Others Vs Muhammad Ismail & Others (2024 CLC 1451) against the person who was not party to the said lis. The above proposition was conclusively settled in the earlier round of litigation in Province of the Punjab’s case3 wherein the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan has held that under Section 79 of the Civil Procedure Code read with Order XXVII, CPC and Article 174 of the Constitution, the suits against the Central Government can be filed in the name of Pakistan (Federation) and against a Provincial Government in the name of the Province. For ready reference, Para-7 of the above said judgment is reproduced as under:- “7. If the trial Court, the appellate Court and the revisional Court had kept in view the requirements of section 79 of the Civil Procedure Code read with Order XXVII, C.P.C. they would not have entertained the claim at all with the parties arrayed in the form in which they were arrayed. Section 79 of the Civil Procedure Code requires, and so does Article 174 of the Constitution, that all suits against the Central Government have to be filed in the name of Pakistan and against a Provincial Government in the name of the Province. Suing Pakistan, as was done in this case, through the Chief Settlement Commissioner and Member, Board of Revenue was in fact not only a mistake but a diversion of the proceedings materially affecting service and representation of the concerned defendants. The Chief Settlement Commissioner had ceased to be a legal entity or a functionary after repeal of the evacuee laws in 1974 --much before the institution of the suit. Provincial Member, Board of Revenue could not represent Pakistan. Similar is the position of Deputy Custodian. There was no functionary of the description of Deputy Custodian after the repeal of the evacuee laws. 3 Province of the Punjab through Member Board of Revenue, (Residual Properties), Lahore & Others Vs Muhammad Hussain through Legal Heirs & Others (PLD 1993 SC 147) As regards the Collector of the District, the procedure prescribed was quite a simple one --a straightforward one, for service on him. It is provided in Order XXVIII of the Civil Procedure Code that the Governments and their functionaries can be served through the Government Pleader. No effort, at any sage, was made to effect service through the Government Pleader, The Clerk of the Court of Chief Settlement Commissioner who made the appearance and even the lawyer appointed by the Solicitor was supposed to represent the Chief Settlement Commissioner when in fact no such office did exist in the eye of law. The revisional Court was in serious legal error in thinking and assuming that Collector represented ex-officio the province of Punjab and by impleading him the Province stood automatically impleaded. Not only the Collector is not under the law representative of Province but in this particular case the Collector was sued as a functionary refusing to give effect to the Registered Deed and not as a representative of the Province. With the parties arrayed as they were, the suit could not be entertained unless necessary correction had been made.” This view has been reiterated in plethora of judgments.4 In Province of Punjab’s case5 the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan has held that:

Therefore, the legislative intent and the purpose of the operation of this provision is for the State, or the Province, to be adequately represented and defended through the impleadment of the proper department. This purpose cannot be achieved if the concerned and proper department is not made a party to the suit, nor can it be achieved if the State, or Province, are not named in the suit.

This Court, in previous matters before it, has held that S.79 of CPC is a mandatory provision where the State, or the Province, was either not impleaded in compliance with S.79 of the CPC, and Article 174 of the Constitution, or the concerned department was not made party to the suit. Reference can be made to the cases of Province of the Punjab through Member Board of Revenue (Residual Properties) v. Muhammad Hussain, Haji Abdul Aziz v. Government of 4 Messrs Fine Electric Corporation Vs. Province of Punjab and 3 others (1989 SCMR 1407) and The Federation of Pakistan Vs. Mir Mohim Khan (PLD 1955 Baluchistan 21), Mst. Maqbool Begum etc. Vs. Gullan & Others (PLD 1982 SC 46) & Muhammad Siddique (Deceased) through L.Rs. and others Vs. Mst. Noor Bibi (Deceased) through L.Rs. and others (2020 SCMR 483) 5 Province of Punjab through Secretary Excise & Taxation Department, Lahore & Others Vs. Murree Brewery Company Ltd (MBCL) & Another (2021 SCMR 305) Balochistan through Deputy Commissioner, Khuzdar, and Government of Balochistan, CWPP&H Department and others v. Nawabzada Mir Tariq Hussain Khan Magsi. 14. Admittedly, the suit/state land is situated within the prohibited zone and the writ petitioners, so called allottees are fighting the battle of litigation in order to usurp the precious /valuable state land which is an urban property, on the basis of concealment of facts and fraud they obtained the order/judgment from this Court without properly assisting and also not produced record that the suit property is situated within prohibited zone and no proprietary rights could be granted which proved that they committed fraud with the Court whereas an alike controversy qua the allotment of state land situated within prohibited zone has already been considered by this Court in Muhammad Israfeel’s case6 and rescinded the allotment and grant of proprietary rights of the state land falling in the prohibitory zone. The supra judgment/order was challenged in Intra Court Appeal (No.37127-2020) as well as a subsequent ICA No.85/2021 titled Mushtaq Ahmad etc. Vs The Province of Punjab etc. along-with other connected ICAs were challenged before the learned Division Bench of this Court but the same were also stood dismissed. Likewise 6 Muhammad Israfeel & Others Vs. The Province of Punjab & Others (2021 MLD 313) another Writ Petition [No.57766/2021] was also dismissed on 05.10.2025 on analogy of the aforementioned judgment of Muhammad Israfeel case [2021 MLD 313]. The said order of dismissal of writ petition was assailed before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan who while dismissing Civil Petition No.1925-L/2021 on 25.08.2022 upheld the supra order of this Court. Thus no proprietary rights of the state land falling in the prohibited zone can be granted at all to any of the claimant. Further reliance is placed on a judgment dated 09.03.2015 rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in Civil Appeal No.693 of 2008 titled as Muhammad Siddique & others Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Water & Power, Islamabad & others and Faiz Ahmad’s case7. And same view has been reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in Muhammad Yousaf’s case8. Thus the bar on the grant of proprietary rights of state land falling in prohibited zone has attained finality whereas under Article 189 of Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, all the state functionaries except the Hon’ble Federal Constitution Court of Pakistan are placed under 7 Faiz Ahmad through legal heirs and others Vs. Chairman Federal Land Commission, Islamabad and others [2024 MLD 756 (D.B)] 8 Muhammad Yousaf and others Vs. Member Judicial-IV, Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore and others (2025 SCMR 459) bounded obligation to comply with judgments of the Hon’ble Supreme Court. 15. It is noticed that in the aforementioned Writ Petitions, the District Bar Association, DG Khan was not party and in Paragraph No.6 of judgment dated 14.12.2010, announced on 21.12.2010 it was observed that the Members of District Bar Association Dera Ghazi Khan appeared and claimed that the official respondents have agreed to transfer resumed state land measuring 471-Kanals 19-Marla to the said Bar Association for establishing the Lawyers Housing Colony. There is no final order passed by the competent authority for the transfer of the property situated within prohibited zone in favour of District Bar Association, DG Khan who is neither party nor any order was ever passed in its favour and nor they filed any petition, as such judgment dated 14.12.2010 [announced on 21.12.2010] passed in Writ Petition No.9372/2010 as well as Para-6 to that extent is against the record. It could not be brought into the knowledge of the Court that District Bar Association, DG Khan is neither lessee nor allottee nor any order ever passed by the competent authority in favour of the District Bar Association. On the basis of concealment of fact with inter se collusiveness of the local authority they obtained judgment from this Court which falls under the definition of concealment of fact and fraud.

Moreover, Bar Association is not lessee under Section 10(3) of the Colonization of Government Land (Punjab) Act, 1912 to pray for transfer of said land to it and nor it was party to the previous litigation regarding the suit land. Thus the suit land cannot arbitrarily doled upon it. Reliance is placed on Province of Punjab’s case9 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan has held as under: “10…. No person shall have any right or title in the State land until a written order has been passed and allottee/grantee has lawfully taken over the possession but in the instant case neither the land was allotted to both the organizations nor they lawfully acquired possession thereof. But the learned High Court has erroneously observed in the impugned judgment that the matter was finally decided between the parties and was concluded/finalized whereas the fact of the matter is that the two Bar Associations were never allotted the land in dispute or delivered its possession. Thus, the argument of the learned counsel for the respondents Bar Associations and the observations of the learned High Court on the letter dated 9-5- 1991 are against the facts as the said letter was written by the Deputy Commissioner, Khanewal by making proposal for such allotment and it cannot be said to be an allotment unless and until it is approved by the competent Authority.” Reliance is also placed on Mian Asghar Ali’s case10, wherein the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan held as under:- 9 Province of Punjab through Secretary revenue and others Versus District Bar Association, Khanewal and others (2014 SCMR 1611) 10 Mian Asghar Ali Vs Govt. of Punjab through Secretary (Colonies) BOR, Lahore & Others (2017 SCMR “4. Review Petitioner challenged the said judgment through Civil Petitions No.2466 to 2468 of 2004, before this Court, wherein leave was declined vide judgment dated 16.12.2004; since reported as Mian Asghar Ali v Province of Punjab through District Collector and others (2006 SCMR 936), operative part whereof is reproduced here in below:- “Independent thereof any intervention with the impugned order would tantamount to encouraging perpetuation of patent illegal devices to protect the illegitimate gains reaped by the political vultures for unjust enrichment at the cost of public exchequer which has eroded the very moral fabric of the society.” 13. We have examined the record with the assistance of Petitioner and learned ASC for the Respondents. As noted in the narrative above, in detail that the order for the cancellation of conveyance deed through private treaty (dated 29.10.1994), was passed by the Member (Colonies) BoR through detailed order dated 4.7.98 (page 78 CPLA NO.2364 of 2015) pursuant to various representation and essentially on the directions made in WP No. 4039 of 1995. Therefore, it cannot be said that the impugned sale was either cancelled on the direction of the Chief Minister or for that matter in dictated exercise of jurisdiction/force command, of the Chief Executive of the Province. It may be observed that it was the Review Petitioner, as observed by this Court, in earlier round culminated into judgment reported as Mian Asghar Ali (Supra) who “exerted political influences with provincial hierarchy got 8 marlas plus prime commercial land situated within the compound of Municipal Committee, Sahiwal from Member BOR, securing relaxation of ban from Chief Minister, Punjab, precipitating in sale deed dated 29.10.1994, in violation of Municipal committee’s Policy keeping the later in darkness” against, which the Civil Review Petitions, were also dismissed as withdrawn and matter of cancellation of conveyance deed for all practical purposes attained finality and a fait accompli. No exception to the cancellation of sale deed obtained by the Review petitioner by misrepresentation and through fraudulent means, by the Member (C) BOR, under section 30(2) of Colonization of Government Land Act, 1912 could now be agitated in subsequent proceedings, founded entirely on different cause of action obliquely. 14. It may not be out of place to mention that the controversy raised by the Petitioner culminating into present Review Petition is not arising out of the order (dated 4.7.1998), of cancellation of sale deed by way of private treaty but, the order dated 16.06.2010 passed by the Member (Colonies) BoR, whereby his request for the allotment of alternate land was declined for valid reasons.” (emphasis supplied)” This view has been reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in plethora of judgments.11

The judgment/order was obtained by the District Bar Association on the basis of concealment of material facts as such it has not come to the Court with clean hands which disentitles it from any discretionary relief.12

Further in Paragraph No.6 of the impugned judgment dated 14.12.2010 [announced on 21.12.2010] it was observed that the representative of the District Bar Association Dera Ghazi Khan appeared and claimed that the respondents have agreed to transfer land measuring 471-Kanals 19- Marlas from the resumed land to Bar Association for establishing the Lawyers Housing Colony. But no application of the Bar for its impleadment as a party in the main writ petition is available in the writ petition and this Court in its suo moto jurisdiction introduced the District Bar Association in its main judgment, whereas this Court has no jurisdiction to pass any order in exercise of its suo 11 Province of Punjab through Collector, Sheikhupura VS Anjuman Talim-ul-Islam and others (PLD 1987 SC 123), Syed Mazhar Hussain Shah through L.Rs VS Member, Board of Revenue, Punjab, Lahore and others (2006 SCMR 959) and Muhammad Manzoor VS Province of Punjab and others (2011 CLC 494 Lahore) 12 Mst. Shahida & Another Vs. Board of Intermediate & Secondary Education, Larkana through Chairman, at Larkana & 5 Others (PLD 2001 SC 26) and Sayed Abbas Taqi Mehdi Vs. Mst. Sayeda Sabahat Batool & Others (2010 SCMR 1840) moto powers but if it is done that will have lack of conformity with the consistent law on the subject whereby a complete embargo is placed upon the suo moto exercise of powers by this Court which powers are not vested in it. Reliance in this regard is placed on a latest judgment dated 20.11.2024 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in Civil Petition No.767 of 2022 titled as Federal Government Employees Housing Authority through its Director General, Islamabad Vs. Ednan Syed and others, the relevant portion whereof is reproduced as under : “12. This Court has consistently ruled that the High Courts do not have suo motu jurisdiction and as such the constitutional scheme never intended to confer such powers on the High Courts. This Court in the Abdullah Jumani judgment, authored by one of us (Muhammad Ali Mazhar, J.), has held that the High Court cannot assume suo motu jurisdiction by overreaching or overstretching its constitutional limits. It is constitutionally impermissible for the courts to expand and enlarge their jurisdictional domain, which is neither allowed by the Constitution nor by the law. In the Taufiq Asif case, this Court has held that the High Court cannot grant a relief, which is not even sought in the petition. As per the Akhtar Abbas case, ‘it is settled law that in writ proceedings, the relief must be confined to the prayer made in the writ petition and the High Court cannot issue a writ suo motu’. Hence, in view of the dictum laid down by this Court, the High Court cannot on its motion declare the policy as unconstitutional and illegal.” (emphasis supplied) In an alike case, an information was received from PSO to the Hon’ble Chief Justice, Peshawar High Court, Peshawar who took cognizance of the matter while sitting in Division Bench and passed judgment dated 26.08.2013 and the said matter reached at the threshold of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan who reversed the said judgment of Peshawar High Court in Dr. Imran Khattak’s case13 holding that the High Court under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 has no authority to exercise suo moto jurisdiction. The relevant portion of the judgment (supra) is reproduced as under: “8……We have, therefore, no hesitation to hold that the High Court could not exercise Suo Motu jurisdiction under Article 199 of the Constitution of Pakistan. The more so when we have noticed that such jurisdiction has stridently been used even in the matters which are clearly and squarely outside the jurisdiction of a High Court.” In another case before the learned Single in Chamber High Court of Quetta an issue was brought before the court regarding two years contract appointment which was challenged and during pendency of said lis the contract period of the employee was expired and the authority extended the said period of service for two years. Learned Single Judge in Chamber set aside the said extension order vide judgment dated 08.11.2017 passed in Writ Petition No.721/2015 but the said judgment was also set aside by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in Jahanzaib Malik’s case14 by holding that first appointment was under challenge whereas subsequent extension was not 13 Dr. Imran Khattak and another Vs. Ms. Sofia Waqar Khattak, PSO to Chief Justice and others (2014 SCMR 122) 14 Jahanzaib Malik Vs. Balochistan Public Procurement Regulatory Authority through Chairman Board of Directors and others (2018 SCMR 414) assailed and the High Court had no power to set aside fresh appointment in exercise of its suo moto jurisdiction. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan while rendering Mian Irfan Bashir’s case15 has held that the learned Single Judge in Chamber while deciding a matter passed observation regarding wearing of helmet, whereas issue before this Court was regarding removal of sign board, as such no direction could not be issued in suo moto qua wearing of helmet by motorcyclists. In another case the High Court, Peshawar took notice of the price escalation of the poultry/dairy products and passed different directions in the said case. The said orders/directions were assailed before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan who while setting aside the aforesaid orders/instructions in case tilted Messrs Sadiq Poultry (Pvt.) Ltd’s16 has held that the High Court has no suo moto power and only Supreme Court of Pakistan under Article 184(3) & 189 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 has power to exercise such jurisdiction. Further reliance is placed on cases wherein the aforesaid view has been maintained in catena of other pronouncements.17 15 Mian Irfan Bashir Vs. The Deputy Commissioner (D.C.), Lahore and others (PLD 2021 SC 571) 16 Messrs Sadiq Poultry (Pvt.) Ltd. Vs. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Chief Secretary and others (PLD 2023 SC 236) 17 Abrar Hassan Vs. Government of Pakistan and another (PLD 1976 SC 315), Akhtar Abbas and others Vs. Nayyar Hussain (1982 SCMR 549), Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif and others Vs. Muhammad Habib Wahab Al-Khairi and others (2000 SCMR 1046), Raja Muhammad Nadeem Vs. The State and another (PLD From perusal of the aforesaid dicta laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan, it is clear in express terms that this Court under Article 199 of Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 has no suo moto jurisdiction to encroach upon the jurisdiction of the executive.

Here in the instant lis no allotment order was ever passed by the competent authority in favour of District Bar Association whereas vide impugned judgment dated 14.12.2010 [announced on 21.12.2010] Revenue authorities were directed to transfer 471-Kanals 19-Marlas land to the Bar Association which is against the law and record as the Hon’ble Judge was not holding any suo moto power under Article 199 of Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973.

In Writ Petition No.9563/2010 titled “Abdul Hakim etc. Vs. Member (Judicial-V) Board of Revenue, Punjab Lahore etc.” writ petitioners have challenged the vires of order dated 11.03.2005, passed by the District Officer (Revenue)/District Collector, DG Khan who observed that as per Para 2(g) of Notification dated 28.05.1995 suit land is needed for public purpose. The suit land falls within prohibited zone and same is excluded from any 2020 SC 282), Taufiq Asif and others Vs. General (Retd.) Pervez Musharraf and others (PLD 2024 SC 610) and Abdullah Jumani and others Vs. Province of Sindh and others (2024 SCMR 1258) grant of proprietary rights, whereas the occupants of the state land falling within prohibited zone cannot claim as a matter of right to necessarily grant them proprietary rights of the state land and under the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912 nobody is authorized to give proprietary rights of the state land situated within prohibited zone. The said order was upheld by the Executive District Officer (Revenue), DG Khan who dismissed the six appeals vide order dated 17.03.2010. Against the above said order Revision Petitions (RORs) Nos.56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 65 of 2010 & No.1290 of 2008 of the private respondents were also dismissed by the Member (Judicial-V), Board of Revenue, Punjab vide order dated 20.08.2010.

Moreover, the property is a state urban property and High Court has no jurisdiction to grant proprietary rights rather under Article 173 (5) of the Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, it is only the government who has the power to transfer said land as per law. For reference Article 173(5) of the Constitution is reproduced as under: “Transfer of land by the Federal Government or a Provincial Government shall be regulated by law.” Under Section 10(3) of the Colonization of Government Land (Punjab) Act, 1912 neither any lease agreement was executed in favour of the Bar Association nor it fulfilled the requisite parameters of an eligible claimant of the state land falling in prohibited zone as such its assertion for allotment of such state land is untenable being perverse, illegal, based on fraud and misrepresentation as the property is situated within the prohibited zone. Further, as regard the allotment and grant of proprietary rights of land measuring 100 Kanal to the Writ Petitioners, suffice it to say that as the land is situated within the prohibited zone as such as discussed above neither it can be allotted to anyone nor its proprietary rights can be granted. Such cases should have been burried at the very inception to save the precious time of the public. Reliance is place on cases titled as S.M.Shafi Ahmad Zaidi through Legal Heirs Vs. Malik Hassan Ali Khan (Moin) through Legal Heirs (2002 SCMR 338) and Haji Farman Ullah v. Latif-ur-Rehman (2015 SCMR 1708).

Moreover under Section 23 of the Contract Act, 1872, if any order is passed by an authority beyond its jurisdiction and against the public policy, such order is nullity in the eyes of law. For ready reference, Section 23 of the Act ibid is reproduced as under: “23. What consideration and objects are lawful and what not.—The consideration or objection of an agreement is lawful, unless—It is forbidden by law; or is of such a nature that, if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law; or is fraudulent; or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another; or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.” (emphasis supplied) With regard to contract being against law and public policy, the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in Hameedullah’s case18 held that:- “From the aforestated observations it is clear that the agreement between the Government and the appellant was in the nature of sale of a public office, consideration being the transfer of land. Sale of public office cannot be a legal transaction. It is completely illegal and against public policy. Therefore, such an agreement is hit by section 23 of the Contract Act, which makes it void.” (emphasis supplied) The August Court in Maulana Abdul Haque Baloch’s case19 has held as under:- “The competent authority also failed to determine the terms and conditions to be fixed in granting the relaxations sought for. In this view of the matter, in absence of the requirements of rule 98 being fulfilled in the instant case, all relaxations were granted in excess of authority and were entirely beyond the scope of the provisions of law, and therefore, ultra vires the powers granted under rule 98 of BMCR 1970 read with section 5 of the Act of 1948, and thus void. Shorn of relaxations so grant, CHEJVA has no legal sanctity and consequently remains an agreement entered into 18 Hameedullah and 9 others Vs. Headmistress, Government Girls School Chokara, District Karak and 5 others (1997 SCMR 855) 19 Maulana Abdul Haque Baloch and others Vs. Government of Balochistan through Secretary Industries and Mineral Development and others (PLD 2013 SC 641) against the provisions of law, hence not enforceable. All the key provisions of CHEJVA were made subject to a reliance on relaxations that were illegal and void ab initio, the illegality of the agreement seeps to its root. As such, no operative part of the agreement survives to be independently enforceable and the principle of severability cannot be applied to save any part thereof. The agreement is, therefore, void and unenforceable in its entirety under the law.” Here in this case the land in question measuring 471 Kanals was ordered to be transferred to the District Bar D.G. Khan notwithstanding the fact that Bar was not party to the earlier litigation. The said allotment was made in sheer violation of Article 173(5) of Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, the express provision of Colonization of Government Land (Punjab) Act, 1912, Section 23 of the Contract Act, and the policy on the subject as well as against the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan.

Further in Para 8 of judgment dated 14.12.2010 passed by this Court announced on 21.12.2010, in which the learned law officer got recorded statement that “out of resumed land measuring 471 Kanals 19 Marla has already been allotted to District Bar Association Dera Ghazi Khan and its possession has already been handed over to them” but he has no authority to make such statement as such his statement is much beyond his authorization and said unwarranted statement cannot be made basis for passing of another alike dictum.20

Further, it is settled law that the proprietary rights of the property situated within prohibited zone cannot be granted and the judgment was obtained by the respondents on the basis of concealment of facts and without properly assisting this Court.

Besides above, the suit property is owned by the provincial government but the provincial government was not made party to the lis. Moreover, the suit state land is situated within prohibited zone and same cannot be allotted to any entity or person. Further, District Bar Association, DG Khan was neither party to the lis nor its any application is available on record of the writ petitions but a huge chunk of state land falling in prohibited zone was ordered to be allotted to it in exercise of suo moto jurisdiction by the Hob’ble Judge which jurisdiction was not available with the Court as discussed above. As the respondents obtained the impugned judgment from this Court on the basis of concealment of facts, fraud, want of jurisdiction and without properly assisting this Court, thus any order 20 Faisalabad Development Authority Vs Raja Jahangir Nasir & Others (2004 SCMR 1247), PLD 2003 Journal 95 (Page 99) obtained through fraud is considered as void, illegal and perverse and same is unsustainable in the eyes of law.

For what has been discussed above, the applications under Section 12(2) CPC (i) C.M.No.3140 of in Writ Petition No.12069/2010, (ii) C.M.No.3138 of 2023 in Writ Petition No.9563/2010 & (iii) C.M.No.3142 of 2023 in Writ Petition No.9372/2010 filed by the applicants are hereby allowed, judgment impugned therein is set aside/ recalled and consequently, the main Writ Petitions No. 12069/2010, No.9563/2010 & No.9372/2010 filed by the writ petitioners are hereby dismissed.
